rubric_additions.rubric-12:
Rule: For selected Node metric settings, preserve the actual owner's supported number parsing, defaults and timeout clamp.
Example: A selected SDK may parse fractional metric timing values and clamp its timeout; an application launch default must not be described as that SDK default.
Evidence: Describe short-run launch defaults as application policy, not SDK behavior.
Insufficient evidence: A replacement parser or assumed default that differs from the actual configuration owner.
rubric_additions.rubric-13:
Rule: Distinguish NodeSDK's native environment setup from direct metric-reader or log-processor constructors.
Example: If otlp,console cannot use the approved local destination, preserve console while isolating only the added OTLP member.
Evidence: If the native path owns metrics, default OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER to otlp only when absent, and prove that the selected SDK registers the expected reader; some compatible releases otherwise create none. Preserve explicit none, empty and other operator values. Keep launch policy separate from SDK defaults. Preserve selected trace/metric opt-outs and actual protocol precedence; an explicitly constructed HTTP exporter or reader does not automatically honor those selectors. Preserve native exporter spellings and distinguish the stricter approved-local branch from SDK fallback for unsupported values. Inspect log-environment reads in both constructor and start. Apply the skip guard before fallback construction and keep it through startup. Restore the exact original operator value in finally even if construction or startup throws; never repeat start after partial global registration. Use the SDK's native exporter-list reader and deduplication. OTLP-only variants, mixed lists, none, empty members, casing and unsupported names must not bypass the added guard. If an OTLP guard or log-only constructor fails, remove only that OTLP member and let the SDK retain the other exporters. Restore the exact original environment value after construction/start and do not retry partially completed global startup.
Insufficient evidence: Guarding only one exporter spelling, overriding an explicit metric opt-out, or retrying start after partial global registration.
rubric_additions.rubric-15:
Rule: For selected Node Resource-only or absent-identity launch tests, account for an active .env/profile that can reload OTEL_SERVICE_NAME.
Example: An active .env file can restore OTEL_SERVICE_NAME after it was removed from the parent environment.
Evidence: Removing that key from the parent environment is insufficient if the profile adds it back. Use isolated configuration copies rather than changing operator settings.
Insufficient evidence: A parent environment change without checking the profile consumed by the real launcher.
rubric_additions.rubric-22:
Rule: Verification: inspect and run the selected checks without editing code.
Example: An SDK console exporter may write after Resource resolution. A selected console bridge must not recapture that SDK output as another application log.
Evidence: For a selected Node setup that combines a console bridge and SDK console exporter, prove that SDK console output is not captured again as application LogRecords. Include selected deferred-Resource resolution or direct-SDK emission paths. Do not add a second or incompatible bridge, or remove the operator's console exporter to hide duplicate records. Reuse a producer proven compatible with the selected setup. Otherwise keep the console-to-OTLP path Not configured/unsupported; constructing processors does not prove application delivery.
Insufficient evidence: Processor construction alone, dropping the operator console exporter, or, when deferred Resource output is selected, testing only an immediate console write.
rubric_additions.rubric-25:
Rule: For selected Node bound-callback restoration tests, let the error actually escape the context scope; catching it inside that scope does not prove restoration afterward.
Example: A bound callback runs with the correct span, then an error escapes. A selected restoration check must inspect the next relevant callback under its own context.
Evidence: Assert the exact span context for every reused bound-callback record. After actual cancellation, schedule and assert the next callback under its own context. Counts or one synchronous outside-context log do not prove these cases. The fixture awaits a Promise completed by setImmediate. Audit plans to verify propagation supplied by the selected Node context manager/runtime. Instrumentation reuses it when it already works instead of adding redundant manual context copying. Verification checks the current real request-to-callback SDK-context join without editing code. Do not assume coverage from the programming language alone.
Insufficient evidence: An error caught inside the same scope, record counts, or one synchronous outside-context log.
rubric_additions.rubric-27:
Rule: For selected Node privacy before capture, an SDK onEmit sanitizer cannot protect native-console output or arguments captured earlier.
Example: An SDK sanitizer can redact its exported copy while Express later prints the original error to the native console.
Evidence: Assess supported Express error middleware and later/default rendering while preserving the response contract, or retain the exact unresolved boundary. If a framework traceback appears during opt-out or another profile, check what that same producer does with the normal bridge enabled. Replay the same source-supported failing request at the selected boundary. Successful-request OTLP logs do not prove privacy on the error-rendering path.
Insufficient evidence: Successful-request OTLP logs used to close privacy on the selected failing error-rendering path.
rubric_additions.rubric-28:
Rule: For the selected Node parser/error path, check native and exported output independently.
Example: A generic redaction label can preserve secrecy while losing the parser error category in exported Body.
Evidence: Preserving the parser category in native output is insufficient if OTLP Body replaces it with a generic redaction label. Preserve the diagnostic category and HTTP status/headers. Keep source-proven inapplicable inputs inapplicable without adding capture.
Insufficient evidence: A native-only category assertion used to claim that the exported category also survived.
rubric_additions.rubric-29:
Rule: If a selected Node local-log processor is built by hand and kept separate from other pipelines, prove that its public options or readers actually use the supported batch log record processor (BLRP) settings.
Example: Leaving constructor options absent proves environment consumption only when the selected public implementation actually reads those settings.
Evidence: Otherwise leave that capability unverified. Omitting constructor options does not prove that the constructor reads environment settings.
Insufficient evidence: Omitted constructor options alone used to claim supported BLRP environment wiring.
rubric_additions.rubric-42:
Rule: Before declaring application fault testing blocked by the Node destination guard, assess a safe, supported fault seam isolated to one process.
Example: An instance-local fault seam can exercise the real application provider without redirecting a shared receiver or global transport.
Evidence: Preserve the real SDK/bootstrap, call sites, actual log-failure responses, healthy other-signal receipts, production guards and shared receivers. Restore test substitutes afterward. If no such seam is available, retain the concrete limitation.
Insufficient evidence: Declaring fault proof blocked without assessing a supported isolated seam, or losing real failure/other-signal observations at that seam.
rubric_additions.rubric-51:
Rule: Selected Node autoconfiguration, manual-reader and processor repairs must use public SDK APIs and their actual owners.
Example: An internal SDK helper may explain list normalization during source inspection without being a supported application import.
Evidence: Reading an internal SDK helper to understand behavior does not authorize importing it into application code.
Insufficient evidence: Importing an internal helper into the application because it was accessible to the reviewer.
